evidence.quote: In this connection, the SFC wishes to remind licensed corporations (LCs) to assess the impact of the Transition on their businesses and take appropriate measures to maintain their smooth and effective operations after the Transition.

authorities.title_or_locator: SFC circular, refNo=24EC16 (official locator in source packet)

claims.action: shorten the standard settlement cycle for transactions in US securities
conditions: Transactions are in US securities, including equities, bonds, exchange-traded funds and options.

evidence.quote: Effective 28 May 2024, the standard settlement cycle for transactions in US securities1 will be shortened from two business days after the trade date (T+2) to one business day after trading (T+1) (the Transition)2.
Such as equities, bonds, exchange-traded funds and options.

claims.statement: The US-securities standard settlement cycle changes from T+2 to T+1 effective 28 May 2024.

claims.action: assess the impact of the Transition on their businesses and take appropriate measures to maintain smooth and effective operations after the Transition
conditions: The Transition affects the LC’s business.

evidence.quote: In this connection, the SFC wishes to remind licensed corporations (LCs) to assess the impact of the Transition on their businesses and take appropriate measures to maintain their smooth and effective operations after the Transition.

claims.statement: LCs should assess the Transition’s business impact and take appropriate measures to maintain smooth and effective operations after the Transition.

claims.action: enhance operational processes, technological infrastructure and systems, and staffing arrangements where appropriate
conditions: Enhancements are appropriate to maintain smooth and effective operations.

evidence.quote: These include enhancing their operational processes, technological infrastructure and systems as well as staffing arrangements where appropriate.

exceptions: Staffing enhancements are qualified by 'where appropriate'.
claims.statement: LCs should consider enhancing operational processes, technology and systems, and, where appropriate, staffing arrangements.

claims.action: assess readiness and ensure ability to cope with the shortened settlement cycle
conditions: The LC conducts US-securities settlement under the shortened cycle.

evidence.quote: LCs should assess their readiness and ensure they are able to cope with the shortened settlement cycle, including:

claims.statement: LCs should assess readiness and ensure they can cope with the shortened settlement cycle.

claims.action: review liquidity risk management practices and ensure necessary funding is available for timely settlement of US securities transactions
conditions: The LC settles US securities transactions.

evidence.quote: Reviewing their liquidity risk management practices and ensuring the necessary funding is available for settling US securities transactions on time.

claims.statement: LCs should review liquidity-risk practices and ensure funding is available to settle US-securities transactions on time.
temporal: On time under the shortened cycle

claims.action: remain mindful of potential liquidity mismatches and settlement failures
conditions: Transactions are cross-currency.
Foreign-exchange settlement remains at T+2 while US-securities settlement is T+1.

evidence.quote: For cross-currency transactions, given that the standard settlement cycle for foreign-exchange transactions remains at T+2, LCs should be mindful of potential liquidity mismatches and settlement failures arising from the different settlement cycles for US securities and foreign-exchange transactions;

claims.statement: For cross-currency transactions, LCs should consider mismatch and failure risks caused by US-securities T+1 versus foreign-exchange T+2 settlement.

claims.action: ensure availability of staff to complete post-trade settlement processes within the shortened timeframe
conditions: Post-trade settlement processes must be completed within the shortened timeframe.

evidence.quote: Ensuring the availability of staff to complete the post-trade settlement processes within the shortened timeframe.

claims.statement: LCs should ensure staff availability sufficient to complete post-trade settlement within the shortened timeframe.

claims.action: adjust staff work shifts, extend working hours, or arrange evening or morning duties, in conjunction with automation
conditions: The LC considers the measures useful to enable timely trade settlements.

evidence.quote: LCs may consider adjusting their staff’s work shifts, extending working hours or arranging evening or morning duties in conjunction with automating their operational processes to enable timely trade settlements.

claims.statement: LCs may consider shift changes, extended hours, evening or morning duties, together with automation, to enable timely settlements.

claims.action: provide adequate training to relevant staff
conditions: Staff are relevant to duties under the shortened settlement cycle.

evidence.quote: Adequate training should be provided to enable relevant staff to effectively perform their duties under the shortened settlement cycle; and

claims.statement: LCs should provide adequate training enabling relevant staff to perform duties effectively under the shortened cycle.

claims.action: proactively engage and communicate with potentially affected clients
conditions: Clients may be affected by the Transition.

evidence.quote: Proactively engaging and communicating with their clients who are potentially affected by the Transition in order to raise their awareness and facilitate their preparations for a smooth transition.

claims.statement: LCs should proactively communicate with potentially affected clients to raise awareness and facilitate preparation for a smooth transition.

claims.action: assess the Transition’s impact on Funds, including settlement-cycle mismatches for subscription money or sale proceeds from non-US markets used to purchase US securities
claims.actor: Management companies of SFC-authorised funds, particularly those with considerable US-securities exposures
conditions: The entity is a management company of an SFC-authorised fund.
The Fund has potentially considerable US-securities exposure.

evidence.quote: In addition, management companies of SFC-authorised funds (Funds), particularly those with considerable exposures to US securities, are reminded to:

Carefully assess the impact of the Transition on their Funds, including any potential mismatches in settlement cycles relating to the deployment of subscription money or sale proceeds from non-US markets to purchase US securities;

exceptions: The heightened emphasis is particularly on Funds with considerable US-securities exposure.
claims.statement: Fund management companies should carefully assess Transition impacts, including mismatches when non-US subscription money or sale proceeds fund US-securities purchases.
temporal: In preparation for and during the Transition

claims.action: make appropriate arrangements, such as expanding pre-funding facilities and allocating additional staff
conditions: Arrangements are necessary to address the compressed settlement timeline.

evidence.quote: Make appropriate arrangements where necessary, such as expanding pre-funding facilities and allocating additional staff to handle the compressed settlement timeline, to ensure that the Funds’ operations remain fair and orderly, and in the best interest of investors; and

claims.statement: Fund management companies should, where necessary, make appropriate arrangements (including possible pre-funding expansion or added staff) to keep Fund operations fair, orderly and in investors’ best interests.

claims.action: give early alerts to the SFC and investors about intended changes, issues or untoward circumstances materially affecting Funds and investors, and take remedial action
conditions: A Transition-related change, issue or untoward circumstance may materially affect the Funds and investors.

evidence.quote: Give early alerts to the SFC and investors about any intended changes, issues or untoward circumstances arising from the Transition that may materially affect the Funds and investors, and take remedial actions accordingly.

claims.statement: Fund management companies should alert the SFC and investors early about materially affecting Transition matters and take remedial action accordingly.
temporal: Early, when the matter arises or is intended

claims.action: monitor market developments relating to the Transition

evidence.quote: The SFC will continue to monitor market developments in relation to the Transition.

claims.statement: The SFC states that it will continue monitoring market developments relating to the Transition.

claims.action: include Canada’s settlement-cycle change within the Transition

evidence.quote: The settlement cycle in Canada will transition to T+1 on 27 May 2024. The reference to the Transition in this circular includes the transition in the US and Canada.

claims.statement: The circular’s defined Transition includes Canada’s move to T+1 on 27 May 2024 as well as the US move.

claims.action: include trade allocation, confirmation and affirmation within post-trade settlement processes

evidence.quote: Including trade allocation, confirmation and affirmation.

claims.statement: Post-trade settlement processes include trade allocation, confirmation and affirmation.

Intermediaries Division                                                             Securities and Futures Commission
Securities and Futures Commission

claims.statement: The circular is issued by the SFC’s Intermediaries Supervision/Intermediaries and Investment Products divisions.
